Week 35 Appendix: A Killing Becomes a Governing Method

Assassination rhetoric hardened into policy this week as courts and resignations held a fragile line against expanding state power.

This week was dominated by the aftermath of Charlie Kirk's assassination, which the administration and its allies used as a pretext for an unprecedented escalation against political opponents, the press, and academic and civic institutions. The FCC chair's explicit threat to revoke ABC's broadcast license over Jimmy Kimmel's commentary—resulting in the show's suspension—represents one of the starkest instances of state coercion of media in the dataset, compounded by Trump's own calls to strip broadcast licenses and designate Antifa a domestic terrorist organization without legal basis. Simultaneously, DOJ leadership pressured a US Attorney out of office for declining to indict Trump's political adversaries (Comey, James), ICE enforcement intensified with fatal shootings, mass raids, and documented inhumane detention conditions, and National Guard deployments expanded to Memphis with threats against Chicago and other cities. Courts, a Georgia judge, and a federal judge dismissing Trump's NYT lawsuit provided some counterweight, alongside continuing congressional pushback and West Coast states countermanding federal vaccine policy.
